doc.title: Dictionary Class
doc.para:
Dictionary Class The Dictionary class is a class for handling dictionary arrays.
A dictionary array is also called an associative array, and is an object that holds multiple pairs of a name and a value linked to it. Like standard arrays, it is accessed using the [ ] (indirect reference) operator, but instead of an index, a string is used, which becomes the name. If the name is a valid identifier, the . (direct reference) operator can also be used. Also, referencing a name that does not exist returns void. To delete an element, use the delete operator.
var d=new Dictionary(); d["sat"] = 1; // Same as d.sat = 1 d["sun"] = 2; // Same as d.sun = 2 d["mon"] = 3; // Same as d.mon = 3 d["name"] ="value!"; // Same as d.name = "value!" d["continue"] = 4; // continue is not an identifier, but OK d.continue = 4; // Error because continue is not an identifier
var sat = d["sat"]; // 1 is assigned var none = d["none"]; // void is assigned
delete d.sat; // Delete sat delete d["continue"]; // Delete continue

Accessing Methods of the Dictionary Class Objects of the Dictionary class do not have any members when newly created. For example, if you want to use the assign method and write dict.assign(src) for a Dictionary class object dict, an error will occur because dict does not possess a method called assign. Therefore, use the incontextof operator to execute methods belonging directly to the Dictionary class using the target Dictionary class object as the context.
var a = %[]; var b = %[]; (Dictionary.assign incontextof a)(b); // Copy b to a (Dictionary.clear incontextof b)(); // Clear the contents of b
saveStruct saveStruct outputs structured data to a file. Please refer to the method of the same name in .

assign The assign method copies a dictionary array.
Syntax : assign(<source dictionary array>, <whether to clear contents=true>)
Copies the contents of another dictionary array specified by the argument entirely. If "whether to clear contents" is false, the contents of the copy destination (the object executing the method) will not be cleared, and the contents of the source dictionary array will overwrite it. If a member with the same name as in the source dictionary array exists in the destination dictionary array, the destination will be overwritten with the content from the source.
If an array (object of the Array class) is specified as the source array, it assumes that the array contains elements that should become members of this dictionary array listed in order of name and value, and copies the contents of that array into this dictionary array.

assignStruct The assignStruct method copies a dictionary array.
Syntax : assignStruct(<source dictionary array>)
Copies the contents of another dictionary array specified by the argument entirely. Unlike the assign method, if members contain an array or a dictionary array, its contents are also copied recursively (in the case of the assign method, only references are copied).
clear The clear method erases all contents of the dictionary array.
